patterns.name: Thin Delegator Pattern for Commands
patterns.description: Commands are 3-line markdown shims with `disable-model-invocation: true` that delegate to a single skill. The skill is the source of truth for behavior; the command is the user-facing entry point. Pattern: frontmatter with description and flag, then single line 'Invoke the {skill} skill'.

examples.content:
---
description: Systematic debugging with root cause investigation
disable-model-invocation: true
---

Invoke the debugging skill and follow it exactly as presented to you

---
description: Test-driven development with Red-Green-Refactor
disable-model-invocation: true
---

Invoke the tdd skill and follow it exactly as presented to you

patterns.applicability: All new commands should follow this pattern unless they are standalone utilities (rare exceptions like /setup-pm) or enriched integrations (rare exceptions like /learn)
benefits: Eliminates code duplication - skill logic in one place
Enables skill evolution without command changes
exceptions: Enriched commands integrate multiple skills (e.g., /learn uses context-compressor + memory protocol)

patterns.name: Systematic Commands Inventory Audit
patterns.context: Commands System Overhaul (Task #83 discovered inconsistent state)
patterns.description: Before refactoring commands, create a comprehensive inventory matrix with: current state (3 working, 7 stubs, 4 dead, 3 special), disposition (keep, convert, delete, create new), target state, dependencies. Matrix prevents hidden dead code and uncovers patterns.
patterns.applicability: For any command system refactor, file inventory audit, or dead code cleanup
benefits: Enables parallel work (developers can see full scope)

patterns.name: Dead Infrastructure Cleanup via Grep Validation
patterns.context: Tasks #84-85 validated removal of dead references
patterns.description: When deleting commands or features that reference old infrastructure, validate removal with grep patterns: checkpoints.log, /todos/ paths, /state/ paths, skills/learned/ references, memory-record.cjs. Pattern: document expected grep results (should be zero matches), verify after cleanup.
patterns.applicability: For any feature that references old infrastructure, after deletion cleanup validation
benefits: Documents what was removed for future reference

patterns.name: Recursive Descent Parser for Safe Expression Evaluation
patterns.context: Tools System Overhaul Phase C (Task #95) - SEC-TOOL-001 Fix
patterns.description: When code needs to evaluate user-controlled expressions (workflow conditions, config DSLs, template logic), NEVER use new Function(), eval(), or regex-based sanitization. Instead, implement a recursive descent parser that only whitelists safe operations: literals (true/false/numbers/strings), comparisons (===, !==, ==, !=, >=, <=, >, <), logical operators (&&, ||, !), parenthesized grouping. The parser rejects anything it doesn't explicitly support.
patterns.why_it_works: 100% safe because undefined behavior defaults to rejection. Attackers cannot embed code in string literals or bypass pattern matching - parser only recognizes safe token types.
patterns.implementation: SafeExpressionParser class in .claude/lib/workflow/decision-handler.mjs (~200 lines). Tokenizer → Parser → Evaluator. Supports boolean algebra for workflow gate expressions.
patterns.test_coverage: 41 security tests (20 malicious rejections, 16 legitimate expressions, 3 context integration, 2 complex conditions) in tests/lib/workflow/decision-handler-security.test.cjs
patterns.applicability: Any expression evaluation: config files, workflow DSLs, template engines, rule engines, policy languages
anti_patterns: new Function('return ' + userInput)() - arbitrary code execution
patterns.extracted_from: Task #95 (SEC-TOOL-001 fix), validated by 41 passing security tests

patterns.name: Consumer Discovery Pattern for File Relocations
patterns.context: Tools System Overhaul Phase C (Task #95) - 8 library modules relocated from tools/ to lib/
patterns.description: Before relocating ANY file, grep the ENTIRE codebase for: (1) the filename (e.g., 'decision-handler'), (2) the directory path (e.g., 'tools/workflow/'), (3) any require() or import() references to the file. Update ALL consumers before committing. Missing even one import breaks the build, often silently.
patterns.why_critical: Relocated files with missed consumer updates cause MODULE_NOT_FOUND crashes. Example: user-prompt-unified.cjs still referenced old router-state.cjs path after relocation, causing crash on every UserPromptSubmit (Task #47).
update_checklist: Update all require() paths to new location
Update all import paths to new location
Test that all consumers still work
patterns.example: Task #95 relocated 8 modules, updated 45+ consumer imports. Full codebase grep caught all references.
patterns.applicability: Any file relocation, library reorganization, directory restructuring
patterns.extracted_from: Task #95 (8 relocations, 45+ import updates), lessons from Task #47 (missed consumer crash)

patterns.name: Tool Catalog as Programmatic Discoverability Aid
patterns.context: Tools System Overhaul Phase D (Task #96) - created tool-catalog.md for 99 tools
patterns.description: Create markdown catalog at .claude/context/artifacts/catalogs/tool-catalog.md with: summary statistics (active/archived/relocated counts), active tools organized by category, wiring status per tool (package.json scripts, skill references, hook references), archived tools section with restoration instructions, relocated tools section with new locations.
patterns.why_valuable: Enables agents and developers to discover available tools, understand what's wired vs reference-only documentation, know where deprecated tools were moved (git history preserved), avoid creating duplicate tools.
structure: Wiring Status column (package.json, skills, hooks, lib/)
Relocated Tools section (old → new path mapping)
patterns.precedent: Follows pattern from skill-catalog.md, template-catalog.md, command-catalog.md, schema-catalog.md
patterns.example: Task #96 created catalog documenting 66 active + 25 archived + 8 relocated = 99 total tools
benefits: Agents can search catalog to find tools for specific capabilities
Archived tools can be restored with full git history
Wiring status shows what's actually used vs documentation-only
patterns.applicability: Any system with 20+ tools/utilities/modules where discovery is a problem
patterns.extracted_from: Task #96 (tool catalog creation), pattern observed in 4 other catalogs
